judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]omponents of the Loan Servicing Fee" paid directly by the borrower is an undefined concept, and the fee is "payable only as interest with respect to such Loan is received" while also accruing, so entitlement and timing are not cleanly separated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.4's introduction makes these fees payable to the Manager while 5.3(f) treats the Loan Servicing Fee as the cap on the Servicer's compensation, so the identity of the payee is inconsistent across the two provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The defined term "Default Fee Percentage" is used to label a payment amount rather than a percentage, a mislabel that matters because 5.3(f) caps compensation by reference to it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.3(f) aggregates the "Default Fee Percentage" with dollar-denominated fees as a compensation cap, so the mismatch between a percentage and an amount surfaces there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]he regular state interest rate payable to the Company" is almost certainly a corruption of "stated interest rate," and as written the benchmark for the Manager's default-interest entitlement is unintelligible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.3(f) uses "Default Interest" as part of the Servicer compensation cap, so the garbled benchmark propagates into that limit; nothing else contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward list of borrower-paid fees; the defined term is merely OCR-mangled rather than substantively unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.6 and 5.7(a) separately provide that Loan Origination Fees remain the Manager's property, which overlaps with the brokerage commissions described here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single short item with a defined label; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the 5.3(f) compensation cap and the rest of 5.4; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]ll costs, fees, and expenses incurred ... by or on behalf of the Company, the Manager or their Affiliates" is a very broad general phrase followed by a non-exhaustive list, and "extraordinary expenses" is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The last sentence excludes Loan Services expenses, which are defined only in 5.3(f), and 5.5(b) then bundles "expenses and indemnifications" into "Permitted Expenses" although indemnification appears only in 5.5(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines "Permitted Expenses" as "the foregoing expenses and indemnifications" although no indemnification appears in the foregoing text — the indemnity is in the following subparagraph — so the defined term's content is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Permitted Expenses" is defined here but never used again anywhere in the Agreement, and 5.5(c) supplies the indemnity this definition appears to reach backwards for.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso is garbled — "such activities did not result from conduct which constitutes willful misconduct or gross negligence in performing ... the Manager's duties" — and the indemnified class ("members, officers, employees, and consultants of the Company") does not include the Manager whose conduct the carve-out measures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4.3 says the Manager owes the Noteholders no fiduciary duties while this clause measures indemnity by the Manager's "duties under the operating agreement," and 5.5(a) makes indemnification expenses a Company Expense borne ahead of Noteholders.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence of roughly 120 words strings together "construction, brokerage, property management or development or similar compensation" with a general catch-all, and the referents of "that is received" and "with respect to which" are hard to pin down.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It routes Loan Origination Fees under 5.7(a) and other payments to the Manager outside the 5.4 fee schedule and the 5.3(f) compensation cap, which is in tension with those limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[F]or which it will receive a brokerage, origination, renewal or forbearance fees from the borrower" has an ambiguous "it" (Company, Manager, Servicer or Affiliate) and a number disagreement, and the amount is "determined on a case-by-case basis."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.6 says the Loan Origination Fee "shall remain the property of the Manager or such Affiliate," while 5.4(e) treats loan brokerage commissions paid to the Company as a Manager fee, so who keeps the fee depends on which provision governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (ii) requires a price "no higher than the independently appraised value" and simultaneously "no lower than the total amount of the Company's investment," a pair that can be impossible to satisfy, and the sub-numbering shifts between (1)/(ii) and (x)/(y); clause (iv) then requires the opposite direction ("no less than the independently appraised value").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (iv) disapplies the whole protective regime for Sponsored Investment Funds and Private Clients, terms defined in 5.1(b)-(c) so broadly that the exception can swallow the rule, and 5.3(d) separately permits such sales in the Manager's sole discretion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]he borrower shall not be default under the loan" is missing a word, and "loan underwriting criteria customarily applied by the Company" is a self-referential standard with no benchmark.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.3(e) permits the Company to purchase loans from the same counterparties "in its sole discretion," and 5.7(e)'s closing paragraph exempts Sponsored Investment Fund borrowers from related-party treatment, both of which qualify these conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The price floor is stated as the greater of unpaid balance or fair market value, which is determinate; "net sales proceeds" is undefined but workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers accurately to 5.7(e)(iii), but 5.3(e) permits the same sales on terms the Manager alone determines, so the two provisions must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The twenty percent cap and the conditions are precise, but the closing paragraph's carve-out for loans to a "Sponsored Investment Fund or a Private Client" is a broad exception that removes the largest likely category from the definition it qualifies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 5.1(c), which names R.E. Loans, LLC as a Sponsored Investment Fund, the carve-out can exempt substantially all affiliate lending from the twenty percent cap, which is difficult to reconcile with 3.7's stated Company purpose and 5.7's protective scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two express conditions, both determinate; "terms no less favorable ... than terms negotiated in an arm's length transaction" is a familiar comparative standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its subordination hierarchy (Company Borrowings, then the Lien) matches 2.3(b) and 5.3(a), so it is consistent with those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]he terms and risk to the Company shall be no less advantageous ... than if such loan ... were made pursuant to an arm's length transaction ... in the same geographical market with comparable property as security" is a multi-factor comparison with no method of proof.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its final sentence subjects Noteholder-Affiliates to 5.7, yet 5.1(a) expressly excludes "any Noteholder" from the Affiliate definition, a definitional pull worth noting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The concluding words — "no provision of this Agreement shall be deemed to prohibit any such person from conducting such other businesses or activities" — are an unbounded override of the rest of the instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6.1(c) requires the Manager's principals to devote such business time as is reasonably necessary to the Company, and 5.7 restricts affiliate dealings, so a clause declaring that no provision prohibits outside activity is hard to square with both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "At such times as the Company has not repaid in full" is awkward but workable; the consent threshold is stated as "Noteholders holding a majority of the aggregate principal amounts of Notes."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6.2 defines "Majority in Interest" as holders exceeding fifty percent, and 6.1's own introduction repeats the covenant period without the consent proviso, so three overlapping formulations of the same threshold and period appear in adjacent provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare lead-in; on its own it is unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates the covenant period from the Article 6 introduction but drops that introduction's "unless Noteholders holding a majority ... consent" escape, so whether 6.1's covenants are waivable by majority consent is left unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[P]romptly upon the issuance of the Notes" is a soft timing standard but the obligation itself is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.3(a) authorises the Manager to grant liens senior to that same security interest and to subordinate it, so the perfection covenant delivers less than it appears to; 6.2(b) also uses "Lien" in a different sense.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The covenant is clear on its face; the opening qualifier "[s]ubject to its discretion to prepay all or a portion of certain Notes" is the only soft element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 1.4(b) lets the Manager prepay selected Notes in its sole discretion and 1.4(c) is itself subject to 1.4(a)-(b), so this ratable-payment covenant may be read as wholly displaced by those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]uch amount of their business time ... as is reasonably necessary to effectively manage the affairs of the Company and the Manager" is a vague and self-defining standard with no measurable floor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.9 entitles the Manager's members and affiliates to engage in unlimited outside business and says no provision of the Agreement prohibits it, which pulls directly against this time-commitment covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It offers a choice between GAAP and "the International Financial Reporting System (IFRS)" — a misnaming of the Standards — at the Company's discretion, and inspection is limited by "reasonable" qualifiers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It grants inspection rights to "the Members and Noteholders" although 4.3 says Purchasers do not become members, so the reference to Members reaches persons outside this Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reporting content beyond tax information is left entirely to the Company's discretion, which makes limb (b) close to unenforceable, though that is a matter of substance rather than ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 1.2(a) separately promises quarterly certification of Loan Amounts on request and permits website posting, which is consistent with the website mechanism here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]ommercially reasonable efforts to prevent the structure ... from constituting an investment in a fractionalized mortgage, interest in a mortgage pool, tenancy in common or other security" pairs a list with a broad catch-all ("or other security").
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.3(c) permits Co-Lending Activities on whatever terms the Manager determines, so this efforts covenant is the only constraint on that discretion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As written the Company affirmatively covenants "[t]o make any mortgage loan" precisely when foreign-secured Portfolio Loans exceed twenty percent — the negative has plainly been dropped, inverting the intended restriction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.7 states the Company's purpose is lending on real property "located primarily in the United States," so read literally this covenant contradicts that purpose statement and the protective intent of Article 6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line catch-all covenant to perform; nothing ambiguous within it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It names the Subscription Agreement, Notes and Security Agreement consistently with 10.7's entire-agreement clause; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It capitalises "Principal" without definition and defines "Majority in Interest" late, in the middle of Article 6, after the concept is functionally used earlier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Article 6 introduction uses "a majority of the aggregate principal amounts" for the same purpose, and 6.3, 9(c) and 10.5 all rely on "Majority in Interest" defined only here, so the thresholds are stated in two different ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short enumerated prohibition with well-understood corporate terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 1.6's maturity extension "to allow for an orderly liquidation of Portfolio Loans" touches the same territory but does not contradict this consent requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It uses "Lien (as defined in the Security Agreement)" for third-party liens although 2.3(b) already defines "Lien" as the Noteholders' own lien, and the sentence lurches from a prohibition into an affirmative defence obligation without a clean break.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.3(a) authorises the Manager to grant senior liens and subordinate the Noteholders' Lien without any Majority in Interest consent, which is squarely in tension with this consent requirement; 9(b) lets the Collateral Agent consent on the Noteholders' behalf.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It conditions the prohibition on months in which a "Portfolio Management Fee" is payable, but no such defined term exists, and "[p]ay directly any salaries or bonuses" leaves indirect payment untouched.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5.4(a) defines the corresponding charge as the "Management Fee" (describing it as a monthly portfolio management fee), so this prohibition's trigger depends on equating two differently defined labels.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[S]ettle any claim that the Company may have against a Member" is broad, and the parenthetical carve-out for a Sponsored Investment Fund attaches ambiguously to "their respective Affiliates."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It protects Noteholders against affiliate-friendly settlements while 5.3(b) and 5.7 permit wide affiliate dealing at the Manager's discretion; the two coexist but the carve-out narrows this protection.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[I]ts sole remaining Manager" is short and clear, though "Manager" is defined in 3.3 as "its manager or managers" collectively, which makes the singular usage slightly off.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3.3's collective definition of "Manager" runs throughout the Agreement, so applying a plural-defined term to a "sole remaining" individual requires a small adjustment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[M]aterially and adversely effects" uses the wrong word, and "the economic interests of the Noteholders" is an undefined and contestable measure of when consent is required.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble makes the Operating Agreement the source of undefined terms and 5.2 permits any use of proceeds "not prohibited by the Operating Agreement," so amendments to that document can move this Agreement's content without triggering an obvious economic-interest test.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It calls the Notes "non-negotiable" while also requiring transfers to be "to qualified investors only," a term used in 1.2(d) but never defined, and consent may be withheld in "sole and absolute discretion."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The securities legend on the signature page contemplates transfer upon an opinion of counsel that an exemption applies, without mentioning the Company's absolute consent right, so the two transfer regimes do not match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (iii) says "to comply with state or federal securities with respect to the issuance of the Notes," omitting the word "laws," and the grant to execute "[t]his Agreement" by attorney-in-fact after the Purchaser has already signed is odd.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It empowers the Manager to execute "any amendments or cancellation" of this Agreement and the Security Agreement, which sits uneasily with 1.5's and 10.5's amendment thresholds requiring Noteholder consent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trailing phrase "for the sole purpose of enabling the Manager to execute ... any instrument necessary to effect such transfer" may limit the whole survival clause or only the assignment limb, and it is unclear whether that limitation cuts back the broad grant in 8.1(a).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8.1(a) grants a much broader authority than the "sole purpose" language here appears to permit on survival, and Section 7 makes assignments ineffective without the Company's consent, so the assignment scenario contemplated is itself conditional.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]ecessary or expedient" and "necessary or appropriate in the judgment of the Manager" are open-ended standards attached to an unlimited class of documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with 4.2's further-assurances covenant and 8.1's power of attorney without contradicting either.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The indemnity sentence is convoluted to the point of obscurity ("the Company does not have an obligation to indemnify the Noteholders or, if the Company does have an obligation ... but is unable to do so"), and "[t]he Manager will appoint" leaves it unclear whether appointment is mandatory or when it must occur.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It makes the Collateral Agent's actions binding on Noteholders and gives its fees priority over them, which pulls against 10.6's cumulative individual remedies and 2.3(a)'s grant of a security interest to the Noteholders themselves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[O]n terms required by Manager" combined with "only to the extent that such terms or actions are not prohibited under this Agreement or the Security Agreement" is a general authority bounded by an unspecified prohibition set.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6.2(b) prohibits liens on the Collateral without a Majority in Interest, yet 5.3(a) authorises the Manager to direct exactly such subordination through the Collateral Agent, so whether the savings proviso bites is genuinely contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substitution condition is conditional and detailed but readable; "unless required by law" is an unspecified escape.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its exclusion of Affiliate-held Notes from the vote is not mirrored in 6.2's or 10.5's Majority in Interest definitions, and 5.1(a) excludes Noteholders from "Affiliate" altogether, which complicates the calculation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The no-third-party-beneficiary rule is stated plainly, subject to "except as expressly provided in this Agreement," which is a self-referential qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Manager, the Servicer, the Collateral Agent and Greenberg Traurig are all non-parties on whom Sections 5.4, 5.6, 9 and 10.8-10.9 confer substantial rights and protections, so this clause is in tension with those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional choice-of-law clause; "as applied to agreements among Delaware residents" is a fiction but a standard one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 10.8(d) measures the conflict waivers against "the California Rules of Professional Conduct or similar and applicable rules in any other jurisdiction," so the governing-law choice and the professional-conduct standard point to different states.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate counterparts clause; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision elsewhere qualifies execution formalities; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It lists delivery methods and deemed-receipt periods but nowhere specifies notice addresses, and "during normal business hours of the recipient" is undefined for a nationwide investor base.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several provisions turn on strict notice periods (1.4(a)(ii)(B) sixty days, 1.6 ninety days, 2.4(a) ten days/24 hours), so the absence of an address regime here matters to those clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence says no modification "shall be effective with respect to all Purchasers unless" approved, which by negative implication leaves open modifications effective as to some; it then permits individual waivers and unilateral Company waivers of timing provisions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 1.5 sets a different amendment regime for the Notes (majority by unpaid principal, with a discriminatory-application proviso), so two overlapping amendment mechanisms with different thresholds govern the same economic terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional non-waiver and cumulative-remedies clause, carefully drafted and internally consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9(a) makes the Collateral Agent's actions binding on the Noteholders and 5.3(a) permits standstill agreements restricting their remedies, which qualifies the "cumulative and not alternative" promise here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It enumerates the integrated documents and adds a no-reliance sentence; the phrase "with regard to the subject matter hereof" is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble incorporates the Operating Agreement (Appendix A) as the source of undefined terms and 5.2 measures permitted use of proceeds against it, yet the Operating Agreement is omitted from this list, and 4.1(b) has Purchasers acknowledge a private placement memorandum also omitted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph is punctuated erratically ("the “Portfolio Transactions.)" and an unclosed quotation at "Company Counsel), and it silently redefines "Noteholder" to include principals, employees, agents and Affiliates for two paragraphs only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That expanded meaning of "Noteholder" conflicts with 1.1's definition tying the term to the record owner of a Note and with 5.1(a)'s exclusion of Noteholders from "Affiliate," and 10.1 disclaims third-party rights that these paragraphs confer on counsel.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The statement that counsel is not and will not represent the Noteholders is unequivocal, though "Company Legal Matters" is defined to include "any dispute that may arise," a broad forward-looking category.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 10.9(a) then has each party consent to Company Counsel representing "one or more Noteholders or their affiliates" in unrelated matters, and 10.9(b) contemplates simultaneous representation of a Noteholder, so the flat disclaimer here does not sit easily with those consents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[E]xcept as otherwise specifically provided by this Agreement" carves out an exception that no other provision supplies, leaving the fee-bearing rule qualified by nothing identifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 9(a) does give the Collateral Agent priority payment for counsel it hires on the Noteholders' behalf, which may or may not be the exception this clause gestures at.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver is expressly of "any present conflict of interest," which raises an obvious question about future conflicts, and it covers representation adverse to the Noteholder "including any dispute between ... the Company and one (1) or more Noteholders" — a one-sided term whose scope would be construed against its drafter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The final sentence subordinates the whole waiver to the California Rules of Professional Conduct even though 10.2 chooses Delaware law, and 10.9(a) grants a broader consent covering future representation, so the temporal scope is unsettled across the two paragraphs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It consents to counsel representing Noteholders "in matters unrelated to the Transactions, including ... matters of a similar nature to the Transactions," a phrase that is close to self-contradictory in delimiting what counts as unrelated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 10.8(b) states flatly that Company Counsel "is not representing, and will not represent, the Noteholders," which points the opposite way from this consent to representing them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines interests by reference to a "Portfolio Loan Transaction" although the defined term elsewhere is "Portfolio Transactions," and the consent is layered with a proviso ("subject to the specific consent of the Noteholder") that partially withdraws the consent just given.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 10.8(b)'s disclaimer of any representation of Noteholders is difficult to reconcile with the simultaneous representation contemplated here, and 10.1 disclaims third-party rights for counsel.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]ot infrequently has simultaneously represented" is imprecise disclosure language, and the paragraph repeats "with their permission" three times while asserting an informed consent whose factual predicate is left general.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its assertion that counsel represented "solely the Company and/or the Sponsored Investment Fund" and not any Noteholder conflicts with 10.9(a)-(b), which consent to representation of Noteholders and their Affiliates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard restrictive legend; its conditions (effective registration statement or satisfactory opinion of counsel) are conventional and determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7 makes transfer impossible without the Company's consent "withheld in its sole and absolute discretion" and requires transfer to "qualified investors," neither of which the legend mentions, so the two transfer regimes state different conditions.
